sounds.name: Analogue Brass
sounds.ref: In the style of early-1980s analogue polysynth brass
sounds.blurb: Bright, swelling brass stabs from two detuned sawtooths.
sounds.how: Two sawtooths a few cents apart beat against each other for width. EG 1 opens the filter with a short swell on every chord, which is what makes a synth sound brassy, and the Basic chorus spreads it out.

steps.title: Two sawtooths, a little apart
steps.why:
VCO 2 joins VCO 1, tuned a few cents sharp.
- MIXER OSC2 70 %: VCO 2 as loud as VCO 1.
- VCO 2 TUNE +15 cents: just off VCO 1, so the two beat slowly.
- Listen for: one sawtooth thickening into a moving, chorused pair.

steps.title: The brass swell
steps.why:
Close the filter and let EG 1 open it on every chord.
- CUTOFF 500 Hz: dark when no envelope is moving it.
- FILTER EG1 MOD 50 %: EG 1 sweeps it open several octaves.
- EG 1 ATTACK 120 ms: the sweep takes a moment: the brass "blat".
- EG 1 SUSTAIN 40 %: it settles part-way down while the chord is held.
- Listen for: each chord swelling bright, then mellowing.

steps.title: Shape the volume
steps.why:
EG 2 gives the chords a soft start and a short tail.
- EG 2 ATTACK 48 ms: a quick fade in, like a breath.
- EG 2 RELEASE 190 ms: the chords ring on briefly after the keys come up.
- Listen for: stabs that breathe rather than click.

steps.title: Widen it
steps.why:
The Basic chorus adds a sense of space.
- CHORUS MIX 40 %: enough chorus to spread the brass.
- Listen for: the chords opening out across the speakers.

context.osc2.tune: How far VCO 2 is detuned from VCO 1: how fast the two beat.
context.vcf.eg1: How far each chord swells open.

tweaks.hear: A hard, instant bite instead of a swell.
The beating stops: thinner and more static.

sounds.name: PWM Strings
sounds.ref: In the style of 1970s string-machine pads
sounds.blurb: A lush string section from two pulse waves whose width sweeps slowly.
sounds.how: With the main wave off, each VCO plays only its pulse. LFO 1 sweeps the pulse width up and down, which makes one oscillator sound like several drifting against each other. A slow attack and release and the Ensemble chorus finish the string sound.

steps.title: Pulse waves alone
steps.why:
Turn both main waves off and both pulses on.
- VCO 1 WAVEFORM None: no lamp lit: VCO 1’s main wave is out.
- VCO 1 PULSE on: VCO 1 plays its pulse alone.
- VCO 1 PULSE WIDTH 30 %: a mid-width pulse, reedy rather than hollow.
- VCO 2 WAVEFORM None: VCO 2’s main wave out too.
- VCO 2 PULSE on: VCO 2’s pulse on.
- VCO 2 PULSE WIDTH 30 %: the same width.
- MIXER OSC2 60 %: VCO 2 a little under VCO 1.
- VCO 2 TUNE −10 cents: a few cents flat, for slow beating.
- Listen for: a thin, nasal buzz, not yet like strings.

steps.title: Sweep the width
steps.why:
LFO 1 moves both pulses’ widths slowly: pulse-width modulation.
- LFO 1 RATE 0.79 Hz: a slow sweep, under a cycle a second.
- VCO 1 LFO1 PWM 40 %: how far VCO 1’s width moves.
- VCO 2 LFO1 PWM 40 %: and VCO 2’s.
- Listen for: the buzz starting to shimmer and swirl like a section.

steps.title: Soften it
steps.why:
A lower cutoff takes the edge off.
- CUTOFF 1.1 kHz: warm, with the top end rolled away.
- Listen for: the swirl staying, the fizz going.

steps.title: Bow it slowly
steps.why:
EG 2 makes the chords fade in and out.
- EG 2 ATTACK 700 ms: each chord swells in.
- EG 2 RELEASE 1.1 s: long tails that overlap the next chord.
- Listen for: chords that rise and melt into each other.

steps.title: Ensemble
steps.why:
The Ensemble chorus runs four lines: the string-machine sound.
- CHORUS TYPE Ensemble: four delay lines instead of two.
- CHORUS MIX 50 %: half chorus, half dry.
- Listen for: the strings growing wide and lush.

context.osc1.lfo1pwm: How much the pulse width swirls.
context.chorus.type: Ensemble is what makes it a string machine.

tweaks.hear: A static pulse: the life goes out of it.

sounds.name: Tri-Saw Bass
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s analogue synth-pop basslines
sounds.blurb: A round, punchy mono bass with its sub-oscillator underneath.
sounds.how: The tri-saw wave is softer than a sawtooth but still has an edge. Sub 1 adds a square an octave down for weight, and a short EG 1 decay on a fairly closed filter gives each note its pluck. Mono mode plays one note at a time, as a bass should.

steps.title: One note at a time
steps.why:
MODE to mono with multi trigger: every note restarts the envelopes.
- MODE Mono, multi trigger: the MT lamp lights.
- Listen for: a single line, each note cutting off the last.

steps.title: Tri-saw and its sub
steps.why:
A softer wave with a square an octave below.
- VCO 1 WAVEFORM Tri-saw: tri-saw: rounder than a sawtooth.
- MIXER SUB1 80 %: Sub 1, an octave down, for weight.
- Listen for: the bass getting deeper and fuller.

steps.title: The pluck
steps.why:
Close the filter, and let a quick EG 1 snap it open.
- CUTOFF 229 Hz: mostly closed.
- RESONANCE 30 %: a little emphasis at the cutoff.
- FILTER EG1 MOD 45 %: EG 1 opens it on each note.
- EG 1 DECAY 75 ms: and closes it again quickly.
- EG 1 SUSTAIN 10 %: almost shut while held.
- Listen for: each note starting with a bright blip and settling deep.

context.mix.sub1: How much low end the sub adds.
context.env1.decay: How long each note’s pluck lasts.

tweaks.hear: The bass loses its bottom octave.

sounds.name: Sync Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of early-1980s hard-sync synth leads
sounds.blurb: A tearing, vocal lead from VCO 2 synced to VCO 1, swept by EG 1.
sounds.how: With SYNC on, VCO 2 restarts every cycle of VCO 1, so its own pitch changes only its tone. EG 1 sweeps VCO 2’s pitch down as each note starts, which is the classic sync rip, and ping-pong echoes bounce it across the speakers.

steps.title: One voice, gliding
steps.why:
Mono with single trigger, and a short portamento.
- MODE Mono, single trigger: one note at a time; legato notes do not restart the envelopes.
- PORTAMENTO TIME 130 ms: a short slide between notes.
- Listen for: a lead line that slides from note to note.

steps.title: Hear VCO 2 alone
steps.why:
Swap the mixer over to VCO 2.
- MIXER OSC1 0 %: VCO 1 out of the mix: it will be the sync master.
- MIXER OSC2 80 %: VCO 2 in.
- Listen for: the same sawtooth, now from VCO 2.

steps.title: Sync it
steps.why:
With SHIFT, VCO 2’s pulse button is SYNC. Lift VCO 2 above VCO 1.
- SYNC on: VCO 2 restarts with every cycle of VCO 1.
- VCO 2 TRANSPOSE +7 st: VCO 2 a fifth up: now this changes the tone, not the note.
- Listen for: a harder, hollower tone at the same pitch.

steps.title: The sync sweep
steps.why:
EG 1 sweeps VCO 2’s pitch as each note starts.
- VCO 2 EG1 MOD 60 %: how far EG 1 pushes VCO 2 up.
- EG 1 DECAY 190 ms: how fast the sweep falls back.
- EG 1 SUSTAIN 0 %: it falls all the way.
- Listen for: each note tearing in with a vocal "yow".

steps.title: Echoes
steps.why:
A ping-pong delay bounces the lead side to side.
- DELAY TYPE Ping-Pong: echoes alternate left and right.
- DELAY TIME 361 ms: about a third of a second apart.
- DELAY MIX 30 %: echoes under the dry lead.
- Listen for: the line answering itself across the speakers.

context.osc2.eg1: How wide the sync sweep is.

tweaks.hear: Just a pitch blip: the tearing tone needs sync.

sounds.name: Mod Wheel Vibrato
sounds.ref: In the style of expressive analogue solo leads
sounds.blurb: A clean lead whose vibrato and wah come in only as you push the mod wheel.
sounds.how: LFO 3 is silent until the mod wheel brings it in. Its LFO3 MOD knobs, under SHIFT, set where it goes, here both oscillators’ pitch and a little of the filter, and its MOD WHEEL knob sets how far the wheel can take it. One wave serves every voice, so a chord wobbles together.

steps.title: A plain lead
steps.why:
Two sawtooths an octave apart.
- MIXER OSC2 50 %: VCO 2 under VCO 1.
- VCO 2 TRANSPOSE +12 st: an octave up, for brightness.
- Listen for: a bright, steady lead with no movement.

steps.title: Set LFO 3
steps.why:
A vibrato speed, and the wheel’s full reach.
- LFO 3 RATE 4.79 Hz: a singer’s vibrato speed.
- LFO 3 MOD WHEEL 100 %: the wheel can bring LFO 3 all the way in.
- Listen for: nothing yet: LFO 3 has nowhere to go.

steps.title: Send it to the pitch and the filter
steps.why:
With SHIFT, the LFO2 MOD knobs become LFO3 MOD.
- VCO 1 LFO3 MOD 25 %: VCO 1’s vibrato depth.
- VCO 2 LFO3 MOD 25 %: the same on VCO 2, so they stay in tune.
- FILTER LFO3 MOD 30 %: a little wah in time with it.
- Listen for: push the mod wheel up: the vibrato grows with it, and goes when you pull it down.

context.lfo3.wheel: How far the mod wheel can bring LFO 3 in.
context.osc1.lfo3: How deep the vibrato is at full wheel.

tweaks.hear: With the wheel up, a trill between two pitches.
A pronounced wah on the wheel.
The wheel only brings in a gentle vibrato.

sounds.name: Unison Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of big analogue unison leads
sounds.blurb: All seven voices stacked on one note for a huge, thick lead.
sounds.how: Unison puts every voice on the note you play, each slightly detuned, so seven pairs of sawtooths beat against each other. A touch of glide and a delay make it sing.

steps.title: Stack the voices
steps.why:
MODE to unison: the Unison and MT lamps light.
- MODE Unison, multi trigger: all seven voices on each note, detuned.
- Listen for: one note turning into a thick, wide chorus of them.

steps.title: Add VCO 2
steps.why:
A second sawtooth in every voice.
- MIXER OSC2 60 %: VCO 2 under VCO 1.
- Listen for: even more weight.

steps.title: Glide and echo
steps.why:
A short slide, and echoes behind it.
- PORTAMENTO TIME 78 ms: the stack slides between notes.
- DELAY MIX 30 %: echoes under the lead.
- Listen for: a lead that soars and trails off.

context.kbd.mode: Unison is what makes it huge.

tweaks.hear: One voice a note: much thinner.

sounds.name: Moving Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of slow-evolving ambient analogue pads
sounds.blurb: A warm tri-saw pad whose filter breathes slowly, all its notes together.
sounds.how: Both VCOs play tri-saw, slightly apart. LFO 2 in Monophonic mode is one wave for every voice, so it opens and closes the filter on the whole chord at once, a slow breath rather than notes moving separately. The Ensemble chorus widens it.

steps.title: Two tri-saws
steps.why:
A softer wave on both oscillators, a little apart.
- VCO 1 WAVEFORM Tri-saw: tri-saw on VCO 1.
- VCO 2 WAVEFORM Tri-saw: and on VCO 2.
- MIXER OSC2 60 %: VCO 2 under VCO 1.
- VCO 2 TUNE +20 cents: just sharp, for slow beating.
- Listen for: a warm, gently moving chord.

steps.title: Fade in and out
steps.why:
EG 2 makes it a pad.
- EG 2 ATTACK 1.6 s: a slow swell.
- EG 2 RELEASE 1.6 s: a long tail.
- Listen for: chords that rise and fade.

steps.title: One slow breath
steps.why:
LFO 2 in Monophonic mode (SHIFT and its wave-shape button), moving the filter.
- LFO 2 MODE Monophonic: one wave for every voice.
- LFO 2 RATE 0.28 Hz: one cycle every few seconds.
- CUTOFF 739 Hz: a darker starting point.
- FILTER LFO2 MOD 50 %: how far LFO 2 opens it.
- Listen for: the whole chord brightening and darkening together.

steps.title: Ensemble
steps.why:
The four-line chorus.
- CHORUS TYPE Ensemble: four lines.
- CHORUS MIX 50 %: half and half.
- Listen for: the pad filling the space.

context.lfo2.mode: Monophonic keeps every note breathing together.

tweaks.hear: Each note breathes on its own, out of step.
A vocal, whistling edge on the sweep.

sounds.name: Clocked Random Bleeps
sounds.ref: In the style of 1970s sample-and-hold sci-fi bleeps
sounds.blurb: A held note turned into random, resonant steps locked to the clock, with synced echoes.
sounds.how: LFO 2 on sample and hold picks a new random level each cycle. In Clock Sync mode the cycle is a note value of the e7’s clock (120 BPM with no MIDI clock), and it moves a resonant filter, so each step is a new bleep. The delay is synced too.

steps.title: A resonant filter
steps.why:
Narrow and singing.
- CUTOFF 739 Hz: low enough for the peak to sing.
- RESONANCE 70 %: a strong, whistling peak.
- Listen for: a held note with a ringing tone.

steps.title: Random steps
steps.why:
LFO 2 on sample and hold, sending the filter.
- LFO 2 WAVE SHAPE Sample and hold: a new random level each cycle.
- FILTER LFO2 MOD 70 %: each level moves the cutoff.
- Listen for: the filter jumping to a new place, at random.

steps.title: Lock it to the clock
steps.why:
With SHIFT, the wave-shape button sets the MODE; RATE then picks a note value.
- LFO 2 MODE Clock Sync: one wave for every voice, on the clock.
- LFO 2 RATE (CLOCK) 1/16 note: a new step every sixteenth note.
- Listen for: the bleeps falling into a steady rhythm.

steps.title: Synced echoes
steps.why:
A ping-pong delay at a dotted eighth.
- DELAY TYPE Ping-Pong Sync: ping-pong, set as a note value.
- DELAY TIME (CLOCK) Dotted 1/8: a dotted eighth: echoes between the steps.
- DELAY FEEDBACK 50 %: several repeats.
- DELAY MIX 40 %: loud enough to fill the gaps.
- Listen for: the pattern multiplying into a busy, bouncing sequence.

context.vcf.lfo2: How far apart the steps jump.

tweaks.hear: A repeating falling sweep instead of random steps.
Each step rings like a struck bell.

sounds.name: Velocity Keys
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s analogue electric-piano-like keys
sounds.blurb: A plucky key sound that grows brighter and louder the harder you play.
sounds.how: VELOCITY EG1 MOD makes the filter’s envelope follow how hard each key is played, and VELOCITY EG2 MOD does the same for the volume. EG 2’s keyboard tracking makes high notes die away sooner, as on a piano.

steps.title: A soft wave with an edge
steps.why:
Triangle on VCO 1, a sawtooth an octave up underneath.
- VCO 1 WAVEFORM Triangle: a soft, hollow triangle.
- MIXER OSC2 30 %: a little VCO 2 for edge.
- VCO 2 TRANSPOSE +12 st: an octave up.
- Listen for: a mellow tone with a little bite.

steps.title: A decaying key
steps.why:
EG 2 shapes a struck note that fades while held.
- EG 2 DECAY 1.1 s: the note fades over a second or two.
- EG 2 SUSTAIN 20 %: to a quiet hold.
- EG 2 RELEASE 300 ms: a short ring after the key comes up.
- EG 2 KEYBOARD TRACKING 60 %: higher notes fade sooner.
- Listen for: notes that strike and fade like a piano.

steps.title: Brightness from your touch
steps.why:
EG 1 opens the filter, scaled by velocity.
- CUTOFF 500 Hz: dark at rest.
- FILTER EG1 MOD 50 %: EG 1 brightens each note’s start.
- EG 1 DECAY 300 ms: and fades back.
- EG 1 SUSTAIN 10 %: almost all the way.
- FILTER VELOCITY EG1 MOD 70 %: most of that depends on how hard you play.
- Listen for: hard chords bright and soft ones mellow.

steps.title: Loudness from your touch
steps.why:
VELOCITY EG2 MOD makes the volume follow velocity too.
- AMPLIFIER VELOCITY EG2 MOD 60 %: soft notes quieter, hard ones louder.
- Listen for: the accented chords leaping out.

context.vcf.vel: How much brightness depends on your touch.
context.vca.vel: How much loudness depends on your touch.
context.env2.kbd: How much sooner high notes die away.

tweaks.hear: High and low notes fade alike.

sounds.name: Key-Synced Wobble
sounds.ref: In the style of 2010s wobble bass
sounds.blurb: A growling bass whose filter wobble restarts on every note and speeds up as it plays.
sounds.how: LFO 2 in KB Sync mode restarts its wave each time a key goes down, so every note wobbles from the same point. Its EG1 MOD (under SHIFT) lets EG 1 speed the wobble up at the start of each note, which works in every mode but Monophonic and Clock Sync.

steps.title: A mono bass
steps.why:
Mono, multi trigger, with two sawtooths and a sub.
- MODE Mono, multi trigger: one note at a time.
- MIXER OSC2 70 %: VCO 2 as loud as VCO 1.
- VCO 2 TUNE +20 cents: slightly sharp, for growl.
- MIXER SUB1 60 %: weight underneath.
- Listen for: a heavy, buzzing bass.

steps.title: The wobble
steps.why:
LFO 2 opens and closes a resonant filter.
- CUTOFF 229 Hz: mostly closed.
- RESONANCE 45 %: a vocal edge.
- LFO 2 WAVE SHAPE Descending ramp: a descending ramp: open, then a falling sweep.
- LFO 2 RATE 3.16 Hz: about three wobbles a second.
- FILTER LFO2 MOD 80 %: a deep sweep.
- Listen for: the bass going "wow-wow-wow".

steps.title: Restart on each key
steps.why:
With SHIFT, LFO 2’s MODE to KB Sync.
- LFO 2 MODE KB Sync: each note starts the wobble from the top.
- Listen for: every note wobbling the same way, in time with the riff.

steps.title: Speed it up with EG 1
steps.why:
With SHIFT, LFO 2’s RATE knob is its EG1 MOD.
- LFO 2 EG1 MOD 50 %: EG 1 quickens the wobble.
- EG 1 DECAY 300 ms: then lets it slow back down.
- EG 1 SUSTAIN 0 %: all the way.
- Listen for: each note starting with a fast flutter that slows into the wobble.

context.lfo2.mode: KB Sync restarts the wobble on every note.
context.lfo2.eg1: How much faster the wobble starts.

tweaks.hear: The wobble runs free and lands differently on each note.
A steady wobble with no flutter.

sounds.name: Warm Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s synth-pop pads
sounds.blurb: Two sawtooths a few cents apart, fading in slowly through a gently closed filter: the plain, warm analogue pad every polysynth is bought for.
sounds.how: A warm pad is mostly three things: two oscillators slightly out of tune with each other, so they beat and thicken; a filter turned down far enough to take the edge off; and a slow attack and release on the volume. The chorus widens it.

steps.title: Two saws, a little apart
steps.why:
Bring VCO 2 in beside VCO 1 and pull them apart.
- MIXER OSC2 70 %: VCO 2 as loud as VCO 1
- VCO 1 TUNE −10 cents: a touch flat
- VCO 2 TUNE +10 cents: a touch sharp
- Listen for: a thick, slowly beating buzz.

steps.title: Soften it
steps.why:
Close the filter part of the way.
- CUTOFF 1.1 kHz: the brightest harmonics gone
- FILTER KEYBOARD TRACKING 50 %: higher notes a little brighter
- Listen for: a rounder, warmer chord.

steps.title: Swell
steps.why:
Slow EG 2, which shapes the volume.
- EG 2 ATTACK 700 ms: each chord fades in
- EG 2 RELEASE 700 ms: and fades out after the keys
- Listen for: chords that breathe in and out.

steps.title: Widen
steps.why:
Bring in the chorus.
- CHORUS MIX 50 %: half chorus
- CHORUS RATE 0.32 Hz: a slow drift
- Listen for: a wide, gently moving pad.

context.osc2.tune: How far VCO 2 sits from VCO 1: the speed of the beating.

tweaks.hear: Faster beating, a richer but sourer pad.

sounds.name: Glass Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s ambient glass pads
sounds.blurb: Soft triangle waves an octave apart that ring on after the keys: a clear, glassy pad with almost no edge.
sounds.how: A triangle has only a few soft harmonics, so a chord of them sounds pure and glassy. VCO 2 an octave up adds shine; a long release and a little delay let the chords hang in the air.

steps.title: Triangles
steps.why:
Both VCOs to triangle, VCO 2 an octave up.
- VCO 1 WAVEFORM Triangle: soft and hollow
- VCO 2 TRANSPOSE +12 st: an octave up
- MIXER OSC2 50 %: quieter than VCO 1
- Listen for: a pure, slightly bell-like tone.

steps.title: Let it hang
steps.why:
A gentle attack and a long tail.
- EG 2 RELEASE 1.6 s: the chord lingers
- Listen for: chords that overlap as they change.

steps.title: Air
steps.why:
A slow, soft echo.
- Listen for: the glass ringing on into the distance.

tweaks.hear: An octave and a fifth: more bell, less pad.

sounds.name: String Machine
sounds.ref: In the style of the 1970s string ensembles (Solina, ARP)
sounds.blurb: A bright sawtooth through the four-voice ensemble chorus: the lush, slightly synthetic sound of a 1970s string machine.
sounds.how: The string machines of the 1970s were simple divide-down organs with one trick: an ensemble chorus that copied the sound several times, each copy drifting in pitch. The e7’s Ensemble chorus does the same to a plain sawtooth. A soft attack and release make it bow.

steps.title: A bowed saw
steps.why:
One sawtooth, a gentle attack and release.
- Listen for: a plain organ-like saw.

steps.title: Ensemble
steps.why:
The chorus does the rest.
- CHORUS TYPE Ensemble: four drifting copies
- Listen for: the saw turning into a shimmering string section.

context.chorus.depth: How strongly the copies drift: the lushness.

tweaks.hear: A thinner, plainer sound: the ensemble is the strings.

sounds.name: Brassy Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of the early-1980s Oberheim pads
sounds.blurb: A fat, bright pad with a soft brassy bloom on every chord: the big detuned polysynth chords of 1980s rock and pop.
sounds.how: The early 1980s pads were two sawtooths per voice, detuned and stacked, with the filter opened a little by its envelope on each chord so it blooms. A slow attack on the filter envelope makes the bloom gentle rather than a stab.

steps.title: Stack the saws
steps.why:
Both VCOs, wide apart.
- Listen for: a big, fizzing chord.

steps.title: The bloom
steps.why:
Close the filter and let EG 1 open it slowly.
- FILTER EG1 MOD 40 %: how far it opens
- EG 1 ATTACK 300 ms: a slow rise
- Listen for: every chord swelling brighter, then settling.

steps.title: Hold
steps.why:
The volume rises a little more gently.
- Listen for: a smooth, full pad.

steps.title: Width
steps.why:
A basic chorus.
- Listen for: the pad spread wide.

sounds.name: Shimmering PWM Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of 1970s polysynth string pads
sounds.blurb: Two pulse waves whose width is swept slowly by LFO 1, each voice at its own phase: a soft, endlessly shimmering pad.
sounds.how: A pulse wave whose width keeps changing sounds as if it were several oscillators drifting apart: pulse-width modulation. With LFO 1 in Polyphonic mode each voice has its own LFO at its own phase, so every note in the chord shimmers differently.

steps.title: Pulses only
steps.why:
Main waves off; the pulses alone.
- VCO 2 TRANSPOSE +12 st: an octave up
- Listen for: a hollow, reedy chord.

steps.title: Sweep the width
steps.why:
LFO 1 moves both pulse widths.
- LFO 1 RATE 0.56 Hz: slow
- Listen for: the chord shimmering as if several instruments played it.

steps.title: Soften
steps.why:
A slower volume and a darker filter.
- Listen for: a soft, moving pad.

context.osc1.lfo1pwm: How far the widths sweep: the depth of the shimmer.

tweaks.hear: Every voice shimmering together: a more regular movement.

sounds.name: Filter Sweep Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of synthwave filter-sweep pads
sounds.blurb: A resonant chord pad whose filter rises and falls very slowly, all the voices together: the long sweeping pads of trance and synth-pop.
sounds.how: A slow LFO on the cutoff turns a held chord into a long rise and fall. In Monophonic mode LFO 2 is one wave shared by every voice, so the whole chord sweeps together, and resonance makes the sweep audible as a moving peak.

steps.title: A resonant chord
steps.why:
Two saws through a resonant filter.
- Listen for: a nasal, ringing chord.

steps.title: One slow sweep
steps.why:
LFO 2, shared by every voice, moves the cutoff.
- LFO 2 MODE Monophonic: one wave for all
- LFO 2 RATE 0.20 Hz: about five seconds a cycle
- Listen for: the whole chord sweeping slowly bright and dark.

steps.title: Hold
steps.why:
A soft attack and release.
- Listen for: a smooth, sweeping pad.

tweaks.hear: Each note sweeping on its own: a churning, uneven chord.

sounds.name: Dark Drone Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of dark ambient drones
sounds.blurb: A heavy, dark bed of sound with both subs underneath and the filter almost closed, swelling in over seconds: tension under a film scene.
sounds.how: Dark pads live in the low mids. Both subs add a square an octave down; the cutoff sits low so only the body is left; a very slow attack means the chord creeps in rather than starting. Long, quiet echoes give it a cavernous space.

steps.title: Weight
steps.why:
Both subs up.
- Listen for: a heavy, buzzing chord.

steps.title: Darkness
steps.why:
Close the filter.
- Listen for: only the body left: dark and thick.

steps.title: Creep in
steps.why:
A very slow attack and release.
- Listen for: the chord creeping in over seconds.

steps.title: A cave
steps.why:
Long, quiet echoes.
- Listen for: a cavernous space around the drone.

tweaks.hear: The drone opening up: more menace, more edge.

sounds.name: Fifths Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of 1970s cosmic synth records
sounds.blurb: Every note sounds with a fifth above it, so single notes become open, hollow chords: the sound of 1980s synth-rock intros.
sounds.how: Transposing VCO 2 by seven semitones puts a perfect fifth over every key. Single notes then sound like power chords, and plain triads turn rich and open. A soft attack and the chorus make it a pad.

steps.title: A fifth up
steps.why:
VCO 2 seven semitones higher.
- VCO 2 TRANSPOSE +7 st: a perfect fifth
- Listen for: every note an open fifth.

steps.title: Soften
steps.why:
A gentle filter and swell.
- Listen for: a hollow, glowing pad.

VCO 2 synced, alone.
- MODE Mono, single trigger: one note at a time; tied notes glide on without restarting
- Listen for: a hard, hollow lead.

steps.title: Sweep
steps.why:
LFO 1 sweeps VCO 2.
- Listen for: the tone sweeping like a voice.

sounds.name: Theremin
sounds.ref: In the style of 1950s science-fiction films
sounds.blurb: A pure, eerie, sliding tone with a wide, nervous vibrato: the theremin of 1950s science fiction.
sounds.how: A theremin has no steps between notes and a hand-made vibrato. A triangle, a very long glide, and a wide LFO 2 vibrato.

steps.title: Slide
steps.why:
Mono, a long glide.
- MODE Mono, single trigger: one note at a time; tied notes glide on without restarting
- Listen for: a pure, sliding tone.

steps.title: Eerie
steps.why:
A wide vibrato.
- Listen for: an eerie, wavering theremin.

sounds.name: Supersaw Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of trance leads
sounds.blurb: A huge, bright, detuned lead with an echo: the supersaw lead of 2000s trance.
sounds.how: Trance leads stacked many detuned saws. Unison does that with all seven voices; a bright filter and a synced delay finish it.

steps.title: Stack
steps.why:
Unison, wide detune.
- Listen for: a huge, shimmering lead.

steps.title: Echo
steps.why:
A synced ping-pong.
- Listen for: a soaring trance lead.

tweaks.hear: An octave on top: thinner and brighter.
A darker, warmer lead for the breakdown.

sounds.name: Funky Mono Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of 1970s funk synth leads
sounds.blurb: A snappy, resonant, slightly squelchy lead with bends: the synth solos of 1970s funk.
sounds.how: Funk synth leads were snappy and vocal: a resonant filter with a quick envelope, a little glide, and multi trigger so every note bites.

steps.title: Snappy
steps.why:
A resonant snap.
- MODE Mono, multi trigger: one note at a time, each restarting the envelopes
- Listen for: a funky, biting lead.

sounds.name: Pan Flute
sounds.ref: In the style of Andean pan pipes
sounds.blurb: A hollow, breathy, wooden flute with a strong puff at the start of each note: a pan flute.
sounds.how: Pan pipes are hollow and very breathy, with a strong puff. A triangle with noise, a soft attack and a brief, strong filter lift.

steps.title: Breath
steps.why:
A triangle and noise.
- MODE Mono, multi trigger: one note at a time, each restarting the envelopes
- Listen for: a breathy tone.

steps.title: Puff
steps.why:
A strong filter lift.
- Listen for: a puff at the start of each note.

steps.title: Mountains
steps.why:
Long echoes.
- Listen for: a pan flute across a valley.

sounds.name: Auto-Wah Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of 1970s funk auto-wah
sounds.blurb: A lead whose filter wahs open and closed on every note, starting fresh each time: an auto-wah.
sounds.how: LFO 1 in KB Sync mode restarts with every key, so each note gets the same filter movement from the start: a wah that follows the playing.

steps.title: A resonant tone
steps.why:
A saw through a resonant filter.
- MODE Mono, multi trigger: one note at a time, each restarting the envelopes
- Listen for: a nasal lead.

steps.title: Wah
steps.why:
LFO 1, restarting on each key, on the filter.
- Listen for: a wah-wah on every note.

sounds.name: Trance Pluck
sounds.ref: In the style of trance
sounds.blurb: A bright, short, detuned chord pluck bouncing in dotted-eighth echoes: the plucked chords of trance breakdowns.
sounds.how: A trance pluck is a bright, detuned chord that decays to nothing in a fraction of a second; the synced echo turns a simple rhythm into a rolling one.

steps.title: Bright and short
steps.why:
Two saws, a fast filter pluck.
- Listen for: short, bright chord plucks.

steps.title: Rolling echoes
steps.why:
A synced ping-pong.
- Listen for: the plucks rolling across the speakers.

context.env1.decay: How long each pluck stays bright.

tweaks.hear: Echoes almost as loud as the plucks.

sounds.name: Synth Harp
sounds.ref: In the style of the concert harp
sounds.blurb: Soft, ringing plucked notes cascading up and down: a synth harp glissando.
sounds.how: A harp string is plucked and rings softly. A triangle and a quiet saw an octave up, a medium decay with no sustain and a long release so the notes overlap.

steps.title: Strings
steps.why:
A triangle and a soft octave.
- Listen for: a clear, soft tone.

steps.title: Pluck
steps.why:
A ringing pluck.
- Listen for: a cascading harp.

sounds.name: Synth Koto
sounds.ref: In the style of the Japanese koto
sounds.blurb: A bright, twanging pluck that mellows as it rings, in a pentatonic scale with small bends: a koto.
sounds.how: The koto’s plucked strings twang brightly, then mellow. A narrow pulse through a resonant filter that EG 1 opens briefly; a little glide gives the bends.

steps.title: Twang
steps.why:
A narrow pulse.
- Listen for: a buzzy pluck.

steps.title: Mellow
steps.why:
A resonant filter, opened briefly.
- Listen for: a bright pluck that softens as it rings.

context.vcf.eg1: How hard each string is plucked.

tweaks.hear: A koto in a wooden hall.

sounds.name: Marimba
sounds.ref: In the style of Central American marimba music
sounds.blurb: Short, woody, hollow notes with a soft knock: a marimba.
sounds.how: A marimba bar gives a short, woody tone. A triangle with VCO 2 two octaves up, very quiet (the bar’s overtone), a short decay and a brief filter knock.

steps.title: A bar
steps.why:
A triangle and a faint overtone.
- Listen for: a soft, hollow tone.

steps.title: Strike
steps.why:
Short.
- Listen for: woody marimba notes.

sounds.name: Kalimba
sounds.ref: In the style of the African mbira and kalimba
sounds.blurb: A soft, high, round plink with a buzz on the pluck: a kalimba thumb piano.
sounds.how: Kalimba tines are high, round and short with a little buzz. A triangle with a sawtooth an octave and a fifth up, revealed only for an instant by EG 1 on the filter.

steps.title: A tine
steps.why:
A triangle with a hidden buzz above.
- Listen for: a round tone with an edge.

steps.title: Pluck
steps.why:
The buzz only on the pluck.
- Listen for: a kalimba plink.

sounds.name: Dotted Echo Guitar
sounds.ref: In the style of U2’s The Edge
sounds.blurb: Clean, bright, picked notes in eighths with a dotted-eighth echo filling the gaps into a shimmering pattern: The Edge’s delay guitar, on a synth.
sounds.how: The Edge plays simple eighth notes into a delay set to a dotted eighth, so the echoes land between his notes and make a rhythm he never plays. A bright pluck and a synced ping-pong delay do it.

steps.title: A picked note
steps.why:
A bright, short pluck.
- Listen for: clean, picked notes.

steps.title: The echo
steps.why:
A dotted-eighth echo.
- Listen for: a shimmering, galloping pattern.

context.delay.div: Where the echoes land between the notes.

tweaks.hear: Echoes on the notes: the gallop disappears.

sounds.name: Glass Pluck
sounds.ref: In the style of IDM resonant plucks
sounds.blurb: A crystalline, ringing pluck where the resonant filter itself pings like struck glass.
sounds.how: A very resonant filter struck by a fast EG 1 sweep rings at its cutoff for a moment. With keyboard tracking the ring follows the notes.

steps.title: A ring
steps.why:
High resonance, tracking the keys.
- Listen for: a glassy ping.

steps.title: Pluck
steps.why:
A short volume.
- MASTER VOLUME 100 %: up: short sounds need it
- Listen for: crystal plucks.

sounds.name: Bubble Pluck
sounds.ref: In the style of 1990s video-game plucks
sounds.blurb: Short, round plucks that blip up in pitch as they start: a bubbly, liquid electronic pluck.
sounds.how: A tiny amount of EG 1 on the pitch, decaying fast, makes each note start a little high and drop into place: a “bloop”.

steps.title: Round
steps.why:
A triangle pluck.
- Listen for: round plucks.

steps.title: Bloop
steps.why:
A pitch blip.
- Listen for: every note blooping in.

sounds.name: Poly Arpeggio
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s synth-pop arpeggios
sounds.blurb: A bright, fast broken-chord pattern bouncing through echoes: the arpeggio behind countless synth-pop songs.
sounds.how: The e7 has no arpeggiator here, so the phrase plays the broken chord; a short pluck and a synced echo make it shimmer.

steps.title: Pluck
steps.why:
A short, bright pluck.
- Listen for: quick, bright notes.

steps.title: Echo
steps.why:
Synced echoes.
- Listen for: a shimmering arpeggio.

sounds.name: Berlin School Sequence
sounds.ref: In the style of Tangerine Dream
sounds.blurb: A hypnotic, repeating sixteenth-note pattern with the filter slowly opening and closing: the sequencer music of 1970s Berlin.
sounds.how: Tangerine Dream built pieces from short sequences repeated for minutes while the filter was slowly turned. A plucky saw plays the pattern; a slow shared LFO turns the filter for you.

steps.title: A plucky saw
steps.why:
A resonant pluck.
- MODE Mono, multi trigger: one note at a time
- Listen for: a ticking pattern.

steps.title: Turn the filter
steps.why:
A slow, shared LFO on the cutoff.
- Listen for: the pattern slowly opening and closing.

steps.title: Space
steps.why:
Echoes.
- Listen for: a hypnotic, cosmic sequence.

sounds.name: Laser Zap
sounds.ref: In the style of 1970s sci-fi film lasers
sounds.blurb: A sharp, falling “pew” of pitch: a sci-fi laser shot.
sounds.how: EG 1 on both oscillators’ pitch at full, with no sustain and a short decay, throws each note up two octaves and drops it fast.

steps.title: Zap
steps.why:
EG 1 on the pitch, fast.
- MODE Mono, multi trigger: one note at a time
- Listen for: falling zaps.

steps.title: Space
steps.why:
Echoes.
- Listen for: a laser battle.

sounds.name: Wind
sounds.ref: In the style of radio-drama wind effects
sounds.blurb: Gusts of wind rising and falling, whistling at the peaks.
sounds.how: Wind is filtered noise whose pitch rises and falls with the gusts. Noise alone through a resonant filter, swept by a slow LFO, and a slow attack.

steps.title: Noise
steps.why:
Noise only.
- Listen for: a hiss.

steps.title: Gusts
steps.why:
A resonant filter swept slowly.
- Listen for: wind gusting and whistling.

sounds.name: Ocean Surf
sounds.ref: In the style of ambient nature recordings
sounds.blurb: Waves breaking and pulling back: noise swelling up and fading on a slow cycle.
sounds.how: Surf is noise whose loudness and brightness swell together. LFO 2, slow and shared, opens the filter and the volume together.

steps.title: Noise
steps.why:
Noise only.
- Listen for: a hiss.

steps.title: Waves
steps.why:
A slow LFO on filter and volume.
- Listen for: waves rolling in and out.

tweaks.hear: Waves that build slowly and crash.

sounds.name: Siren
sounds.ref: In the style of police-drama sirens
sounds.blurb: A rising and falling siren.
sounds.how: LFO 1 on the pitch, slow and deep, sweeps the note up and down.

steps.title: Wail
steps.why:
A deep LFO on the pitch.
- MODE Mono, multi trigger: one note at a time
- Listen for: a wailing siren.

sounds.name: Random Bubbles
sounds.ref: In the style of BBC Radiophonic Workshop bubbles
sounds.blurb: Random blips of pitch, each voice bubbling on its own: a computer thinking, or a pot boiling.
sounds.how: LFO 1 on Sample and hold takes a new random level each cycle; on the pitch it makes random notes. In Polyphonic mode each voice bubbles on its own.

steps.title: Random pitch
steps.why:
S&H on the pitch.
- Listen for: random bubbling notes.

steps.title: Space
steps.why:
Echoes.
- Listen for: bubbles bouncing around.

sounds.name: UFO
sounds.ref: In the style of 1950s science-fiction films
sounds.blurb: A wobbling, hovering tone that slowly rises and falls: a flying saucer.
sounds.how: Two LFOs at once on the pitch: LFO 1 fast for the wobble, LFO 2 slow for the hover.

steps.title: Wobble
steps.why:
LFO 1 fast on the pitch.
- MODE Mono, multi trigger: one note at a time
- Listen for: a fast wobble.

steps.title: Hover
steps.why:
LFO 2 slow on the pitch.
- Listen for: the saucer rising and dipping.

sounds.name: Alarm
sounds.ref: In the style of sci-fi alarms
sounds.blurb: A harsh, two-tone, fast beeping alarm.
sounds.how: LFO 1 on Pulse flips the pitch between two notes; a narrow pulse wave makes it harsh.

steps.title: Two tones
steps.why:
A square LFO on the pitch.
- MODE Mono, multi trigger: one note at a time
- Listen for: a two-tone alarm.

steps.title: Beep
steps.why:
LFO 2 chops the volume.
- Listen for: a harsh, beeping alarm.

sounds.name: Bird Chirps
sounds.ref: In the style of synthesized birdsong
sounds.blurb: Quick, high, rising chirps: birds in a garden.
sounds.how: Birdsong is fast pitch sweeps. A high triangle with a quick EG 1 attack and decay on the pitch, and short notes.

steps.title: Chirp
steps.why:
EG 1 sweeps the pitch.
- Listen for: quick, rising chirps.

steps.title: Garden
steps.why:
Echoes.
- MASTER VOLUME 100 %: up: short sounds need it
- Listen for: birds calling across a garden.

sounds.name: Explosion
sounds.ref: In the style of film sound design
sounds.blurb: A loud burst of noise that rumbles away into the low end: an explosion.
sounds.how: An explosion is noise that starts bright and loud and decays into a low rumble. EG 1 sweeps the filter down from open; EG 2 decays slowly; the subs add the rumble.

steps.title: Noise and rumble
steps.why:
Noise and the subs.
- Listen for: a roar.

steps.title: Blast
steps.why:
EG 1 sweeps the filter down.
- Listen for: a blast rumbling away.

context.env1.decay: How long the blast takes to rumble away.

sounds.name: Spaceship Drone
sounds.ref: In the style of sci-fi film spaceship drones
sounds.blurb: A low, humming, shifting drone: a spaceship’s engine room.
sounds.how: A low chord of two saws with a sub, a tritone apart, through a resonant filter moved by a slow random LFO.

steps.title: Hum
steps.why:
Saws and the sub, low.
- Listen for: a low, beating hum.

steps.title: Machinery
steps.why:
A random LFO on a resonant filter.
- Listen for: machinery shifting.

sounds.name: Rain
sounds.ref: In the style of ambient nature recordings
sounds.blurb: Pattering noise, random little bursts: rain on a window.
sounds.how: LFO 1 on Sample and hold, fast, on the volume chops noise into random patters; a high filter keeps it crisp.

steps.title: Noise
steps.why:
Noise only.
- Listen for: a hiss.

steps.title: Patter
steps.why:
Random chops on the volume.
- Listen for: rain pattering.

sounds.name: Engine Revving
sounds.ref: In the style of synthesized engine effects
sounds.blurb: A buzzing motor revving up as each key is held and falling back on release: an engine.
sounds.how: A low pulse buzzes; EG 1 slowly raises its pitch while the key is held and lets it fall on release; LFO 1 adds the engine’s judder.

steps.title: A motor
steps.why:
A low pulse.
- MODE Mono, multi trigger: one note at a time
- Listen for: a buzzing motor.

steps.title: Rev
steps.why:
EG 1 raises the pitch slowly.
- Listen for: the engine revving up and down.

steps.title: Judder
steps.why:
LFO 1 on the volume.
- Listen for: a rough engine.

sounds.name: Heartbeat
sounds.ref: In the style of thriller-film heartbeats
sounds.blurb: A deep, muffled “lub-dub” once a second.
sounds.how: Two quick, deep thumps: a triangle with its sub, a little pitch drop and a dark filter.

steps.title: Thump
steps.why:
A deep triangle with a pitch drop.
- MODE Mono, multi trigger: one note at a time
- Listen for: a deep heartbeat.

sounds.name: Synth Kick
sounds.ref: In the style of the TR-808 kick
sounds.blurb: A punchy electronic kick drum.
sounds.how: A kick is a low tone that starts high and drops fast. EG 1 on both oscillators’ pitch, a fast decay, and a short volume.

steps.title: Kick
steps.why:
A triangle, its pitch dropping.
- MODE Mono, multi trigger: one note at a time
- Listen for: a punchy kick.

context.env1.decay: How long the pitch drop takes.

sounds.name: Synth Snare
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s electronic snares
sounds.blurb: A snappy electronic snare: a tonal thud with a burst of noise.
sounds.how: A snare is a drum tone plus the rattle of the wires. A triangle with a pitch drop for the body, noise for the wires, both short.

steps.title: Body and wires
steps.why:
A triangle and noise.
- MODE Mono, multi trigger: one note at a time
- Listen for: a thud with a hiss.

steps.title: Snap
steps.why:
Short.
- MASTER VOLUME 100 %: up: short sounds need it
- Listen for: a snappy snare.

context.mix.noise: How much wire rattle there is.

tweaks.hear: A snare in a big room.

sounds.name: Hi-hat
sounds.ref: In the style of the TR-808 hi-hat
sounds.blurb: Crisp, ticking hi-hats in sixteenths.
sounds.how: A hi-hat is a very short burst of very high noise. Noise only, high resonance on a high cutoff, and a tiny decay. Higher velocity makes the accents louder.

steps.title: Tick
steps.why:
Noise, short.
- Listen for: crisp, accented hats.

tweaks.hear: Every hat the same: more mechanical.

sounds.name: Tom Fill
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s electronic drums
sounds.blurb: A tumbling, pitch-swept tom fill: the “pew” toms of 1980s pop.
sounds.how: Electronic toms sweep their pitch down sharply. A triangle with EG 1 on the pitch and a medium decay; the phrase plays down the toms.

steps.title: Toms
steps.why:
A triangle with a pitch sweep.
- Listen for: a pitch-swept tom fill.

sounds.name: Hand Clap
sounds.ref: In the style of the TR-808 hand clap
sounds.blurb: A papery clap on two and four, from noise flammed by a very short echo.
sounds.how: A clap is several hands not quite together. A short, mid-range noise burst sent into the shortest delay with feedback repeats into a flam.

steps.title: Smack
steps.why:
Noise, mid-range, short.
- Listen for: a short smack.

steps.title: Flam
steps.why:
The shortest delay.
- MASTER VOLUME 100 %: up: short sounds need it
- Listen for: a clap.

sounds.name: Cowbell
sounds.ref: In the style of the 808 cowbell
sounds.blurb: The clanky, two-tone cowbell of 1980s drum machines.
sounds.how: The classic drum-machine cowbell is two square waves at an inharmonic interval, band-limited and short. Two pulses about a fifth and a bit apart.

steps.title: Two squares
steps.why:
Two pulses at an odd interval.
- MODE Mono, multi trigger: one note at a time
- Listen for: a clanky tone.

steps.title: Clank
steps.why:
Short.
- Listen for: a cowbell.

sounds.name: Conga
sounds.ref: In the style of Afro-Cuban congas
sounds.blurb: Round, ringing hand-drum tones in a Latin pattern.
sounds.how: A conga’s skin rings at a pitch with a small drop. A resonant filter pinged by EG 1 with a little pitch drop.

steps.title: Skin
steps.why:
A resonant ping.
- MASTER VOLUME 100 %: up: short sounds need it
- Listen for: ringing hand drums.

sounds.name: Claves
sounds.ref: In the style of Cuban son claves
sounds.blurb: Short, high, woody clicks in a son clave rhythm.
sounds.how: Claves are two hardwood sticks: a short, high, woody click. A triangle high up, a very short decay.

steps.title: Click
steps.why:
A very short, high triangle.
- MODE Mono, multi trigger: one note at a time
- MASTER VOLUME 100 %: up: short sounds need it
- Listen for: woody clicks.

sounds.name: Metallic Hit
sounds.ref: In the style of industrial metal percussion
sounds.blurb: A harsh, clanging metal hit: industrial percussion.
sounds.how: Sync with a big EG 1 sweep on VCO 2 gives a burst of shifting harmonics: a clang. Noise adds the scrape.

steps.title: Clang
steps.why:
Sync, swept.
- MODE Mono, multi trigger: one note at a time
- Listen for: a metallic clang.

steps.title: Hit
steps.why:
Short, with an echo.
- Listen for: industrial hits.

sounds.name: Tremolo Keys
sounds.ref: In the style of a vintage reed electric piano
sounds.blurb: A bright, slightly barking electric piano with a gentle tremolo: the reed piano of 1960s soul.
sounds.how: A reed electric piano is brighter and barkier than a tine piano, with a built-in tremolo. A narrow pulse and a triangle, a quick filter bark, a decaying tone and LFO 1 on the volume.

steps.title: Bark
steps.why:
A thin pulse with a quick bark.
- Listen for: a barking electric piano.

steps.title: Tremolo
steps.why:
A shared LFO on the volume.
- Listen for: a soulful tremolo.

sounds.name: Celesta
sounds.ref: In the style of late-Romantic celesta
sounds.blurb: Soft, high, ringing, bell-like notes: a celesta.
sounds.how: A celesta strikes steel plates: soft, high and bell-like. Triangles an octave apart, keys up an octave, a ringing decay.

steps.title: Plates
steps.why:
Triangles an octave apart.
- Listen for: a soft, ringing celesta.

sounds.name: Music Box
sounds.ref: In the style of the mechanical music box
sounds.blurb: Tiny, high, glassy notes ringing out: a music box.
sounds.how: A music box plucks a steel comb: very high, small, bell-like notes. A triangle two octaves up with a long ring and a slight wobble.

steps.title: A comb
steps.why:
A high triangle.
- Listen for: tiny ringing notes.

steps.title: Worn
steps.why:
A slow wobble.
- Listen for: an old music box.

tweaks.hear: A music box in an empty room.

sounds.name: Gospel Organ
sounds.ref: In the style of gospel organ
sounds.blurb: A full, swirling organ with a fast vibrato and chorus: the church organ of gospel music.
sounds.how: Gospel organ is full and swirling. Square pulses an octave apart, both subs, chorus and a quick vibrato standing in for the rotating speaker.

steps.title: Drawbars
steps.why:
Square pulses and both subs.
- Listen for: a full organ.

steps.title: Swirl
steps.why:
Vibrato and chorus.
- Listen for: a swirling gospel organ.

sounds.name: Rave Organ Stab
sounds.ref: In the style of early-1990s rave
sounds.blurb: A short, bright, minor-chord organ stab with a pitch blip: the rave stab of early-1990s hardcore.
sounds.how: The rave stab is a short minor-seventh chord with a hard attack and a little pitch blip. Square pulses, EG 1 on pitch and filter, short.

steps.title: Stab
steps.why:
Pulses with a blip.
- Listen for: hard rave stabs.

steps.title: Hall
steps.why:
Echo.
- Listen for: stabs across a warehouse.

sounds.name: Hoover
sounds.ref: In the style of early-1990s rave
sounds.blurb: A huge, dark, swooping, chorused growl that bends down into each note: the rave “hoover”.
sounds.how: The hoover is detuned pulse-width-modulated saws in unison, bending down into each note, with a heavy chorus. Unison, a long PWM, EG 1 bending the pitch down, and ensemble chorus.

steps.title: Unison
steps.why:
All voices, saw and pulse.
- Listen for: a huge, churning growl.

steps.title: The swoop
steps.why:
EG 1 bends the pitch into each note.
- Listen for: each note swooping in.

steps.title: Ensemble
steps.why:
Heavy chorus.
- Listen for: the hoover.

sounds.name: Lush 80s Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of mid-1980s polysynth pads
sounds.blurb: A bright, lush, wide pad with a slow bloom, PWM and ensemble chorus: the glossy pads of mid-1980s pop.
sounds.how: The glossy 1980s pad is a saw and a modulated pulse, an ensemble chorus, a slow filter bloom and long release.

steps.title: Saw and pulse
steps.why:
A modulated pulse beside the saw.
- Listen for: a moving, rich chord.

steps.title: Bloom
steps.why:
A slow bloom.
- Listen for: chords blooming.

steps.title: Gloss
steps.why:
Ensemble and echo.
- Listen for: a glossy 1980s pad.

sounds.name: Space Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of space-ambient pads
sounds.blurb: A soft pad whose filter steps to a new place every so often, each step echoing: a pad that seems to twinkle.
sounds.how: LFO 2 on Sample and hold, slow, moves a resonant filter to a new random place a couple of times a second; long echoes let each step ring.

steps.title: A pad
steps.why:
Two saws, soft.
- Listen for: a resonant pad.

steps.title: Twinkle
steps.why:
A slow S&H on the filter.
- Listen for: the pad twinkling.

tweaks.hear: Every note twinkling on its own.

sounds.name: Industrial Bell Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of Depeche Mode
sounds.blurb: A cold, metallic, bell-like lead line with a sync bite: the sampled-metal melodies of mid-1980s Depeche Mode, on an analogue synth.
sounds.how: Depeche Mode built melodies from sampled metal. Hard sync with VCO 2 well above VCO 1 makes a clangy, metallic tone; a quick decay makes it strike like metal.

steps.title: Metal
steps.why:
VCO 2 synced well above VCO 1.
- MODE Mono, multi trigger: one note at a time
- Listen for: a clangy, metallic tone.

steps.title: Strike
steps.why:
A decaying note.
- Listen for: a cold, metallic melody.

sounds.name: Sequenced Octave Bass

sounds.blurb: A heavy bass where every note has its fifth above it: a power-chord bass.
sounds.how: VCO 2 seven semitones up turns a bass line into power chords.

steps.title: Fifths
steps.why:
VCO 2 a fifth up.
- MODE Mono, multi trigger: one note at a time
- Listen for: a power-chord bass.

context.osc2.transpose: The interval above each bass note.

sounds.name: Hollow Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of ambient hollow pads
sounds.blurb: A soft, hollow, woody pad, like a choir of recorders.
sounds.how: A triangle under a square pulse an octave up: both have only odd harmonics, so together they sound hollow.

steps.title: Hollow
steps.why:
A triangle and a square an octave up.
- Listen for: a hollow, woody pad.

sounds.name: Rave Echo Stab
sounds.ref: In the style of 1990s rave
sounds.blurb: One short, bright chord thrown into a ping-pong echo: a riff made from a single hit.
sounds.how: A single stab into a ping-pong delay with high feedback becomes a whole rhythmic figure.

steps.title: A stab
steps.why:
Short and bright.
- Listen for: a short chord.

steps.title: A riff
steps.why:
Ping-pong, high feedback.
- Listen for: one hit becoming a riff.

sounds.name: Soft Square Bass
sounds.ref: In the style of synth-pop square bass
sounds.blurb: A round, hollow, soft bass: good under gentle music.
sounds.how: A square through a closed filter is round and hollow; no envelope on the filter keeps it soft.

steps.title: Round
steps.why:
A square, filtered.
- MODE Mono, multi trigger: one note at a time
- Listen for: a soft bass.

sounds.name: Bright Saw Chords
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s synth-pop chords
sounds.blurb: Bright, buzzing, full chords with the filter wide open: the raw sound of a polysynth.
sounds.how: Two saws, the filter fully open: every harmonic of every note.

steps.title: Raw
steps.why:
Wide open.
- Listen for: bright, raw chords.

sounds.name: Bowed Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of ambient bowed leads
sounds.blurb: A lead that swells into each note, like a bowed instrument.
sounds.how: A slow attack on EG 2 makes every note swell in.

steps.title: Swell
steps.why:
A slow attack.
- MODE Mono, single trigger: one note at a time, tied notes gliding
- Listen for: a swelling, bowed line.

sounds.name: Pulse Arpeggio
sounds.ref: In the style of 1970s Berlin-school sequences
sounds.blurb: A fast, thin, clicky arpeggio of pulse plucks.
sounds.how: A narrow pulse pluck, very short, played as a fast broken chord.

steps.title: Click
steps.why:
A thin pluck.
- Listen for: a fast, clicky arpeggio.

sounds.name: Octave Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of synthwave octave leads
sounds.blurb: A bright, ringing lead doubled an octave up.
sounds.how: VCO 2 an octave up adds a bright edge to a lead.

steps.title: Octaves
steps.why:
VCO 2 an octave up.
- MODE Mono, single trigger: one note at a time, tied notes gliding
- Listen for: a bright, ringing lead.

tweaks.hear: An octave below: a heavier lead.

sounds.name: Random Filter Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of Berlin-school random filter patterns
sounds.blurb: A held chord whose filter jumps to a new random place on every eighth note.
sounds.how: LFO 2 on Sample and hold in Clock Sync mode steps the cutoff in time with the clock, so a held chord becomes a rhythm.

steps.title: A chord
steps.why:
A resonant pad.
- Listen for: a resonant chord.

steps.title: Steps
steps.why:
S&H on the clock.
- Listen for: the chord stepping in rhythm.

sounds.name: Brass Pad
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s polysynth brass pads
sounds.blurb: Warm, held brass chords that swell gently: a pad with a horn colour.
sounds.how: A slow filter blare on two saws, held: halfway between brass and pad.

steps.title: Brass pad
steps.why:
A slow blare.
- Listen for: warm brass chords.

sounds.name: Dark Pluck
sounds.ref: In the style of minimal techno plucks
sounds.blurb: A short, dark, muted pluck: a minimal techno stab.
sounds.how: A low cutoff with a quick, small envelope: dull and percussive.

steps.title: Muted
steps.why:
A dark pluck.
- Listen for: muted, dark plucks.

sounds.name: Vowel Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of 1980s synth-funk talking leads
sounds.blurb: A lead that slowly changes vowel, “oo” to “ah” and back.
sounds.how: A resonant filter in the voice range, moved slowly by LFO 2, changes the vowel as notes are held.

steps.title: A vowel
steps.why:
A resonant filter.
- MODE Mono, single trigger: one note at a time, tied notes gliding
- Listen for: a vocal lead.

steps.title: Talk
steps.why:
A slow LFO on the cutoff.
- Listen for: the lead changing vowel.

sounds.name: Soft Sine Keys
sounds.ref: In the style of lo-fi hip-hop keys
sounds.blurb: Very soft, pure, gently decaying keys: almost a sine-wave piano.
sounds.how: Triangles through a lowered filter are nearly sine waves; a gentle decay makes them keys.

steps.title: Pure
steps.why:
Triangles, soft.
